dropped.claim: Herc Holdings executed a transformative $4.8B acquisition of H&E in June 2025, driving revenue 22.6% to $4.4B but depressing net income from $211.0M to $1.0M through $199M in transaction costs, $156M in additional interest expense from 6.7% weighted average debt facilities, and $48M loss on the divested Cinelease business. While management states H&E integration disruption stabilized in Q3 2025, the combined business faces execution risk as direct operating expenses deteriorated from 40.5% to 42.5% of rental revenue due to lower fixed cost absorption from market moderation and integration challenges, rental equipment sales margin compressed from 28% to 18% on fair value markups and auction channel mix, and pro forma equipment rental revenue declined 6% year-over-year in markets where H&E was concentrated. The business demonstrates resilient cash generation with $1.1B operating cash flow and 21.2% FCF margin despite near-zero accounting profits, but the $2.75B in new senior notes at 7.00% and 7.25% materially increases leverage for a cyclical equipment rental business heavily exposed to construction and industrial end markets navigating elevated interest rates and economic uncertainty.

While management states integration disruption stabilized in Q3 2025 and the $199M transaction costs and $48M Cinelease loss are one-time charges, the organic business momentum, synergy realization progress, and leverage profile require monitoring before the investment case becomes compelling.
